newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian farmers clash with police in milk protest.
newsitem.headline: Italian farmers clash with police in milk protest.

text.p: Italian dairy farmers clashed with police in Milan on Thursday and paralysed other northern cities in angry protests over strict European Union milk output quotas.

Milk producers with tractors broke through a cordon of police in riot gear on the outskirts of Milan and gathered in a central square near the main railway station, while other scuffles broke out around the city perimeter.
Meanwhile, demonstrating farmers with columns of around 500 tractors descended upon north-eastern Padua blocking routes into the city centre and paralysing traffic, police said.
Another 200 farmers demonstrated in Reggio Emilia.

The protests centred on substantial "super levy" fines that EU dairy farmers face for producing too much milk. Estimates from member states place Italy as the worse offender for exceeding its national quota.

Late last year, an EU Commission official said EU milk production was 1.1 million tonnes over quota, with Italy accounting for nearly half the overproducton put at 470 million tonnes. The fines hit individual farmers and not the state.
